subject: Post-demo: latency thresholds and hosting trade-offs — next steps
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@acme-commerce.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: latency thresholds and hosting trade-offs — next steps

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we all have the same frame for the hosting decision (Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC):

Summary of requirements you called out:
- Primary flow: checkout fraud-check + personalization call in the critical path (single-token small completion).
- SLOs: p50 <= 80 ms, p95 <= 250 ms end-to-end for the critical path.
- Typical request shape: ~40 tokens output, sparse context (~100 tokens).
- Traffic: steady baseline ~1,000 req/s with predictable daily peaks to ~3,000 req/s for ~20–30 minute windows.
- Data: no strict on-prem restriction today but SOC2/audit evidence required.

Immediate hosting trade-offs (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest time-to-value, transparent SLAs for small teams, good for bursts if you accept occasional routing latency to other regions. Might struggle on predictable cost at sustained 1k+ req/s unless we recommend batching/caching.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools give predictable latency and unit cost at sustained traffic. Stronger fit given your steady 1k baseline + frequent bursts; allows tuning (int8 quant, kernel selection, batching policy) to hit p95 targets without frequent fallbacks.
- Private VPC/on-prem: appropriate if you must keep egress inside your network or need strict encryption/HSM controls. From our call it sounds optional for phase 1.

Recommendation: pilot on Dedicated with a Hosted fallback for peak bursts. Pilot scope below — attaching a sample traffic file and a starter pilot-config.csv for your infra team.

Pilot proposal (2-week):
- Dedicated pool sized for sustained 1k req/s with headroom to autoscale to 2.5k req/s (burst cap).
- Canary traffic slice (5%) routed through Dedicated to validate p95 at the real request shape.
- Runtime suggestions: int8 quantization for model variant, batching window 8–16 tokens, aggressive KV prefix caching for repeated prompts.
- Observability: per-route latency breakdown, token-level cost, and a quality regression check against your checkout test prompts.

Asks / next steps:
1) Sarah / DevOps: share a 24h traffic sample (JSON) and the IP allowlist constraints — we have traffic-sample-20261127.json attached.
2) Redwood: provide a Dedicated pilot quote and expected p95 numbers for your profile; Ben will draft.
3) Align on start date — earliest we can provision Dedicated pool is 9 business days from confirmation.

Attachments: pilot-config.csv (starter), traffic-sample-20261127.json

Thanks — I’ll loop Ben on the technical bench estimates.

—
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: latency thresholds and hosting trade-offs — next steps

Thanks Jasmine — that summary is right on. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 1k req/s baseline is for the checkout microservice only; other non-critical flows add another ~200 req/s. We care most about p95 for checkout (user-visible).
- Average output tokens per checkout request is 38; 95th percentile token length is ~120.
- Bursts are typically 20–40 minutes, correlated to flash promotions; we can accept short degradation during tail of bursts but want core p95 during baseline and short spikes.

We attached a 24h sample. Cost sensitivity: we need a rough TCO estimate for the pilot (2-week) and an annualized delta between Hosted-only and Dedicated-committed. Can Ben include a ballpark in the pilot quote?

Also, we have an internal security checklist — SOC2 evidence is required before production. Private VPC is a possibility for later.

Sarah

Thanks — reviewed the traffic sample. Preliminary technical appendix (high level):

- Dedicated sizing: a 4-GPU pool (A100-class equivalent) with continuous-serving runtime tuned to int8 quant and kernel selection should comfortably handle a sustained 1k req/s for the checkout model (avg 38 tokens) with the following bench: p50 ~ 45–60 ms, p95 ~ 140–200 ms depending on batching window. We estimate cost-per-request on Dedicated will be ~30–40% lower than Hosted for sustained baseline traffic.
- Burst handling: configure autoscale to add capacity up to ~2.5k req/s; keep Hosted API route available for overflow routing to avoid provisioning extreme headroom. Overflow policy: route excess beyond autoscale to Hosted with synthetic headers so you can trace fallbacks.
- Runtime knobs: batching window 8–16 ms, request grouping by sequence length, prefix KV-caching for repeated user-contexts. Recommend aggressive token-level caching for repeat checkout patterns.
- Quality: int8 quant shows negligible quality regressions on your short-completion prompts in our internal evals; will include prompt-set regression check in pilot.

I attached the benchmark-matrix.csv with microbench results and a starter pilot-config.csv. For the pilot quote: I’ll generate two line items (Dedicated pilot + Hosted fallback) and Hosted-only pilot; include annualized extrapolation for committed pool pricing.

Ben
